note: K31 with the artifact's line endings changed and nothing else, and it pins which of two readings of `verbatim` this package means. `digest_of` strips trailing whitespace and every reader — `read_text` on the working tree, `blob_text` on a blob — goes through universal newlines, so a passage lifted out of a CRLF file is digest-true against an LF copy of the same text and byte-false against the file it came out of. That is the intended reading: a project that normalizes its line endings, or a checkout on another platform, has not falsified anything any entry holds. The seed exists so that a change to any of those readers has to move this outcome before it lands.
history: apply commits/01, commits/02, … as successive commits in a fresh repository; expectations name the commit they apply to. `@commitNN` in an entry is substituted with the real short object id of that commit before it is made, because a seed cannot know an id the runner has not created yet
